tools.name: redbeam_get_state
tools.description: What REDBEAM has open: `file` is the PDF showing (`fileOpen` false on the start screen), `tabs` the PDFs open beside it, and `note` says what to do next. REDBEAM has no projects, so `projectOpen` is always false; that is not a fault.

tools.name: redbeam_project_summary
tools.description: Counts of documents, pages, scopes, markups and calibrated pages for the PDF showing in the window, whose takeoff is read from the PDF itself. Fails, rather than counting zeros, when no PDF is open.

tools.name: redbeam_open_file
tools.description: Open a PDF drawing set in REDBEAM, the way double-clicking it in Explorer does: it comes forward in the window already showing it, fills an empty window, or gets a window of its own. Its takeoff is read from the PDF itself. Returns {accepted:true} — NOT "opened": rendering a large set takes a few seconds, so poll redbeam_get_ui_state until activeDocumentId is set and pageCount is above zero before drawing or reading quantities.

path.description: Absolute path to a .pdf on this computer.

tools.name: redbeam_list_documents
tools.description: Documents in the PDF showing in the window (Light: one document, the PDF). Capped; `truncated` says when there are more.

tools.name: redbeam_list_pages
tools.description: Pages, optionally for one document. page_number is ZERO-based. `label` is only the PDF's own page label and is often empty; redbeam_list_sheets gives the sheet number and title for every page of the open document.

tools.name: redbeam_list_scopes
tools.description: Scopes in the PDF showing in the window. Archived scopes are hidden unless asked for.

tools.name: redbeam_list_markups
tools.description: Markups, filterable by page, scope or document. Soft-deleted markups are excluded unless includeDeleted is set — they are kept for audit and are not live takeoff.

tools.name: redbeam_get_calibration
tools.description: Calibration per page, as feet per PDF point. Without one, no quantity is in feet.

tools.name: redbeam_execute_query
tools.description: Run one read-only SELECT against the takeoff of the PDF showing in the window (the same tables a project database has). Writes are refused: a write here would change a takeoff with no undo entry and no activity row.

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH statement. No semicolons.

tools.name: redbeam_get_ui_state
tools.description: What the window is showing: active document and page, tool, active scope, zoom, selection, open panels, and the computed quantities and piece counts. Needs a window — fails if none is open.

tools.name: redbeam_screenshot
tools.description: PNG of the sheet. With no `region`: the window's canvas as it is, raster and markup overlay composited. With `region`: a close-up of that box of the sheet rendered fresh by PDFium at `width` pixels, sharp at any zoom — use it to read a tag, a note or a dimension rather than cropping a whole-sheet screenshot. Find the box with find_text or get_words. Needs a window with a document open.

overlay.description: Include REDBEAM's markup overlay. Default true for the whole-canvas shot; for a region it follows what the window shows (see set_markup_visibility).

region.description: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top — the space find_text and get_words report boxes in. A 0.05-wide box on an E-size sheet is about 2.5 inches of paper.

width.description: For a region: the resolution, as output width in pixels (height follows the box). Default 1200; 600-800 is plenty to read a tag, 2000+ for fine print. At most 6000.

page.description: For a region: ZERO-based page to show first. Defaults to the open sheet.

annotations.description: For a region: draw the PDF's own markups. Defaults to what the window shows.

tools.name: redbeam_list_sheets
tools.description: Every page of the open document with its sheet number and title ("A4.0", "FLOOR PLAN - LEVEL 03"), from the PDF's bookmarks, then its page labels, then the title block printed on the sheet. `sheet` is null where none of them names the page. Use the page numbers here (ZERO-based) for go_to_page, find_text and screenshot. Needs a window.

tools.name: redbeam_find_text
tools.description: Where text is on the sheets of the open document: every match with its page (ZERO-based), sheet number and box in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y down. Pass a box to redbeam_screenshot `region` for a close-up, or to zoom_to_region to show it. Searches every page unless `page`, `pages` or `fromPage`/`toPage` narrow it; a long set may come back with `notSearched` pages to ask for again. Needs a window.

wholeWord.description: Only whole words, so "C-7" does not also find C-70. Default false.

tools.name: redbeam_set_markup_visibility
tools.description: Hide or show markups for a clean look at the drawing, as the palette's "Hide the PDF's own markups" and "Hide REDBEAM markups" do. `embedded` is the PDF's own annotations (Bluebeam's or anyone's); `redbeam` is the takeoff, dimensions and layout REDBEAM draws over the sheet. Nothing is written or deleted, and the window tells the person while markups are hidden, so show them again when done. Needs a window.

embedded.description: false hides, true shows. Omit to leave as is.

redbeam.description: false hides, true shows. Omit to leave as is.

tools.name: redbeam_measure
tools.description: Measure a distance, or an area, between points on the open sheet, at its scale (a scale region's if the points sit in one, else the sheet's). Nothing is drawn or written. Points are NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y down, the same space find_text, get_lines and screenshot regions use. Without a scale it answers in PDF points and says so. Needs a window.

closed.description: Close the shape and give its area too.

page.description: ZERO-based page to show first. Defaults to the open sheet.

tools.name: redbeam_get_lines
tools.description: The drawing's own line segments inside a box of the open sheet, longest first (or sorted by position): each segment's ends (NORMALIZED [0,1], y down) and its length in PDF points and, when the sheet has a scale, in feet. Read from the PDF's vector paths. Use it to measure a wall, a ceiling grid or a panel off the drawing itself. Filter to lines fully inside the box, horizontal or vertical, or a length range; a segment drawn twice is returned once. Keep the box small. Needs a window.

inside.description: For get_lines: only lines with both ends inside rect. Default false (lines crossing it are included).

angleTolerance.description: For get_lines orientation, in degrees. Default 1.

dedupe.description: For get_lines: merge a segment drawn twice, in either direction. Default true.

sort.description: For get_lines: longest first (default), left to right, or top to bottom.

maxLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out longer segments, in PDF points.

minLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: shortest length kept, in feet.

maxLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: longest length kept, in feet.

tools.name: redbeam_save_copy
tools.description: Save a working copy of the open PDF beside it, with everything the open file holds, and leave the original untouched. REDBEAM keeps takeoff inside the PDF, so before creating scopes or setting a scale on a file that is not yours to change (a client's tender set, someone else's markups), save a copy, open it with redbeam_open_file, and work there. Returns the copy's path. Needs a window.

name.description: File name for the copy. Defaults to "<name> (takeoff).pdf".

withoutEmbeddedMarkups.description: For save_copy: leave every other app's markups (Bluebeam's, anyone's) out of the copy. Links stay. Default false.

tools.name: redbeam_get_bom
tools.description: The bill of materials — what to ORDER, per scope: the deliverable a takeoff exists to produce, computed from the same roll-up the panel renders. Read `confidence` per line before quoting any number: a `blocked` line carries quantity null (the scope is missing something, and 0 would be a claim), and an `unverified` line is a count this build has never checked against the Qt original. `totals` deliberately sums VERIFIED lines only, so it does not agree with adding the rows up — a total that mixes a checked number with an unchecked one hides which is which. Needs a window. Empty until pages are calibrated.

tools.name: redbeam_export
tools.description: Produce the takeoff package. `tsv` is the pricing sheet and `report` is the branded self-contained HTML; both come back as TEXT in the reply rather than as a saved file, because the buttons hand a blob to the browser's downloader and put it somewhere an agent can neither read nor choose — write the string yourself if you want a file. `marked-pdf` is the exception: it writes the OPEN drawing with its markups on it and lands in the user's downloads, so it reports only whether it was written, and it covers one document, not the project. Needs a window. The ESTIMATE exports — `csv`, `estimate-tsv` and `pdf` — cover one round: every scope with its measured quantity and its components. csv and estimate-tsv return content; pdf renders the branded document with a picture of every sheet that carries takeoff and saves it to downloads. With `path`, any format is written to that file instead (its folder must exist; nothing is replaced unless overwrite, never a PDF). pieces-csv is the piece list of every run product.

what.description: tsv, report, csv and estimate-tsv return content; marked-pdf and pdf save a file to the user's downloads and return {saved:true}.

estimateId.description: For csv, estimate-tsv and pdf: which round. Defaults to the open one.

path.description: For export: an absolute path to write the file to, e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\Desktop\\takeoff.csv. Its folder must exist. Without it, text formats come back in the reply.

overwrite.description: For export with path: replace a file already there. A PDF is never replaced.

tools.name: redbeam_describe_product
tools.description: Every input a product needs before it can be counted: for each field its key, the key its unit goes in, label, whether it is required, the units or values allowed, and the default; plus an example specification. Without productType, all products. A blocked BOM line also lists the missing keys under `missing`.

productType.description: For create_scope, update_scope and describe_product: panels, planks, baffle_cassette, baffle, linear_parts or custom_assembly. Decides what the scope is measured as, so create_scope needs no scopeType with it. describe_product without it lists every product.

tools.name: redbeam_set_pattern_origin
tools.description: Set where an area's pattern starts: at a point, a corner, the nearest point on an edge or line, the centre, or back to automatic. Applies to the area at `point`, to markupId(s), or to every area of the scope on the sheet showing. Read it back with redbeam_get_pattern. Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

mode.description: For set_pattern_origin: point (start exactly at `point`, inside the area), corner (the area's corner named by `corner`, or the one nearest `point`), edge (the point on the area's edge nearest `point`, so the first member sits on that edge or line), center (the middle of the area), auto (clear it; the layout chooses the best start).

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

tools.name: redbeam_set_pattern_direction
tools.description: Set the direction the members run, for the whole scope, the sheet showing, or one area, as two points along a member (x1,y1,x2,y2, normalized) or an angle. Area beats sheet beats scope. Laid-out products count nothing until a direction is set. Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

applyTo.description: For set_pattern_direction: the whole scope (default), every area of the scope on the sheet showing, or one area (markupId or point). Area beats page beats scope.

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

angle.description: For set_pattern_direction instead of x1..y2: the direction members run, in degrees on the sheet: 0 across, 90 up it.

tools.name: redbeam_get_pattern
tools.description: A scope's pattern set-up: product type, scope direction, sheet directions, and for each area the direction it uses (and where from) and its origin (placed or automatic). Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

tools.name: redbeam_trace_area
tools.description: The closed boundary around a point inside a field (a hatched ceiling, a room), read from the drawing's own lines, as normalized rings ready for create_markup, with its area. create:true places it as an area. Needs a window.

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

page.description: ZERO-based. For go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area and read_scale; for track_addenda, the addendum sheet when linking by hand.

create.description: For trace_area: also place the outline as an area of scopeId (or the active scope). Default false: the rings are returned for create_markup.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

bridgeGapFeet.description: For trace_area: the widest gap in the linework still treated as closed, in feet. Default 3.5.

tools.name: redbeam_detect_pattern
tools.description: Read a drawn pattern of parallel members (baffles, planks, slats) in a box: direction (and a directionLine for set_pattern_direction), on-centre spacing, member length, runs across and rows along, and how regular it is. Needs a window.

rect.description: For begin_scale_region, zoom_to_region and get_words: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points — the same space find_text reports boxes in. For begin_scale_region, a region carries its own scale for the details sheet where four details sit at four scales; drawing it is only half the gesture — it governs nothing until set_region_scale answers the picker it opens. For get_words, only the words whose centre is inside. For get_lines, the box to read linework from; keep it small.

page.description: ZERO-based. For go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area and read_scale; for track_addenda, the addendum sheet when linking by hand.

minLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out segments shorter than this, in PDF points. Default 2 (hatching and text strokes).

tools.name: redbeam_read_scale
tools.description: The scales the sheets state (title block and under each drawing title), each with its preset id for set_page_scale/set_region_scale and where it is printed, beside the scale set on the sheet and its regions. With `points` and `dimension`, checks the set scale against a written dimension and gives the scale it implies. Defaults to the sheet showing. Needs a window.

page.description: ZERO-based. For go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area and read_scale; for track_addenda, the addendum sheet when linking by hand.

pages.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: explicit ZERO-based page numbers in the OPEN document. set_page_scale defaults to the open sheet and writes them in ONE transaction: half a range carrying a new scale and half the old one is a set where some sheets measure and some do not, with nothing saying which. find_text defaults to every page.

fromPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: start of an inclusive ZERO-based range.

toPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: end of an inclusive ZERO-based range.

points.description: For measure: two or more {x,y} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y down. Nothing is drawn or written.

dimension.description: For read_scale: a written dimension, e.g. 12'-6", to check the sheet's scale against; give the two ends it spans as `points`.

tools.name: redbeam_track_addenda
tools.description: Sheets of the open set replaced by a later issue (the same sheet number later in the set, or linked by hand with page and replaces), and the scopes with takeoff on a replaced sheet. Links are kept in the PDF. Needs a window.

page.description: ZERO-based. For go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area and read_scale; for track_addenda, the addendum sheet when linking by hand.

replaces.description: For track_addenda with `page`: the ZERO-based page this addendum sheet replaces, to link the two by hand.

tools.name: redbeam_create_markups
tools.description: Add several markups in one call and one undo step: each {kind, rings, scopeId?, page?} as create_markup takes them, including holes, arcs (bulge) and circles. A cutout cuts the areas under it, including ones made earlier in the same call. Needs a window.

markups.description: For create_markups: up to 500 entries, each {kind, rings, scopeId?, page?} as create_markup takes them. One undo step.

tools.name: redbeam_get_piece_list
tools.description: A run product's piece list: every run with its length and pieces, each piece's cut length and whether it is cut to fit at an edge or curve, the cutting list (identical cuts counted), stock lengths used by size, offcut, rails, and parts (connectors, end caps, joiners, trim). export what:"pieces-csv" writes it as a sheet. Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

limit.description: For find_text (default 300 matches), get_words (default 3000 words) and get_lines (default 300 lines). get_history: default 200 events. get_piece_list: default 1000 runs.

tools.name: redbeam_get_history
tools.description: Who changed what in this PDF's takeoff and when: markups drawn, edited, moved to a scope or deleted, scopes made and changed, scales set, each marked person or AI app. Kept in the PDF, so it covers earlier sessions. `id` narrows it to one markup or scope. Needs a window.

id.description: For delete_markup, reassign_markup and delete_scale_region. Region ids are reported as `scaleRegions` by redbeam_get_ui_state and nowhere else. For get_history: only this markup or scope.

limit.description: For find_text (default 300 matches), get_words (default 3000 words) and get_lines (default 300 lines). get_history: default 200 events. get_piece_list: default 1000 runs.

tools.name: redbeam_invoke_ui_action
tools.description: Drive the app the way a person would. Navigation and reads: set_tool, set_active_scope, go_to_page, set_layout_preview, open_panel, get_scale_presets, get_bom, export. Reading the sheets: list_sheets (sheet number and title per page), find_text (where text is, with boxes), get_words (every word on a page with its box), zoom_to_region (frame and mark a box in the window), set_markup_visibility (hide the PDF's own markups and/or REDBEAM's for a clean look; nothing is written). Measuring without drawing: measure (distance or area between points at the sheet's scale), get_lines (the drawing's own line segments in a box). Working on a copy: save_copy (a copy of the open PDF beside it, the original untouched; withoutEmbeddedMarkups leaves other apps' markups out). Setting a product up: describe_product (every input a product needs: key, unit key, units, default). Patterns: set_pattern_origin, set_pattern_direction, get_pattern. Reading the drawing: trace_area (the closed outline around a point), detect_pattern (spacing, member length, runs and rows of a drawn pattern), read_scale (scales the sheets state, and a check against a written dimension), track_addenda (sheets replaced by a later issue, and scopes on them). Writing many: create_markups (one call, one undo step). Output: get_piece_list (runs, cut lengths, stock use, parts), get_history (who changed what and when; kept in the PDF). Takeoff writes: create_markup, delete_markup, set_calibration, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction. Setting a takeoff up: create_scope, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope, set_page_scale, begin_scale_region, set_region_scale, cancel_scale_region, delete_scale_region. Saving an answer now (the app also saves each scope by itself once a change settles): commit_scope. Everything goes through the same handlers a click uses, so writes land on the undo stack with an origin of `agent` and are broadcast to other windows — a takeoff change is never invisible to the person who owns it. THE EXCEPTIONS, by name: commit_scope is a RECORD rather than an edit and is superseded rather than undone; set_page_scale, begin_scale_region/set_region_scale and delete_scale_region are project setup that the undo stack has never covered, for the buttons either — so a scale written over a range CANNOT be taken back, and overwriting one nobody asked you to change silently re-measures every markup on those sheets. Read the existing scale first.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

page.description: ZERO-based. For go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area and read_scale; for track_addenda, the addendum sheet when linking by hand.

panel.description: For open_panel. The panels exclude each other, so this closes whichever was open; `none` closes them all. It does NOT dismiss a calibration form — that holds a measurement and has its own Cancel.

what.description: For export: tsv, report, marked-pdf, csv, estimate-tsv, pdf or pieces-csv. See redbeam_export.

estimateId.description: For export csv, estimate-tsv and pdf: which round. Defaults to the open one.

label.description: For create_scope and update_scope, the name on the shelf — must be unique, because two scopes with one label are indistinguishable everywhere it matters and rescoping into the wrong one is silent. For set_region_scale, what the region IS ("Detail 3 / head").

scopeType.description: For create_scope and update_scope. A scope counts only the markup kind it is typed for, so changing it on a scope that already has takeoff does not convert that takeoff — it stops it reaching any quantity.

color.description: For create_scope and update_scope. CSS hex.

specifications.description: For create_scope and update_scope: the product spec. On update it is MERGED, never replaced — this same object also carries the pattern directions the direction tool writes, and replacing it would silently re-orient every piece count on the scope. Set a key to null to remove it.

archived.description: For archive_scope; default true. Archiving hides a scope, it does not destroy it — its markups stay and un-archiving restores the quantities exactly.

presetId.description: For set_page_scale and set_region_scale: a named title-block scale, e.g. `arch-1-8`. Call get_scale_presets — the ids are not guessable and a stated scale needs no measuring, so this covers a whole sheet series where the reference-line tool covers one page.

feetPerPoint.description: For set_page_scale and set_region_scale, instead of presetId: drawing feet per PDF point. Prefer presetId when the title block states a scale, so the stored source records that it was stated, not measured.

pages.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: explicit ZERO-based page numbers in the OPEN document. set_page_scale defaults to the open sheet and writes them in ONE transaction: half a range carrying a new scale and half the old one is a set where some sheets measure and some do not, with nothing saying which. find_text defaults to every page.

fromPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: start of an inclusive ZERO-based range.

toPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: end of an inclusive ZERO-based range.

rect.description: For begin_scale_region, zoom_to_region and get_words: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points — the same space find_text reports boxes in. For begin_scale_region, a region carries its own scale for the details sheet where four details sit at four scales; drawing it is only half the gesture — it governs nothing until set_region_scale answers the picker it opens. For get_words, only the words whose centre is inside. For get_lines, the box to read linework from; keep it small.

kind.description: For create_markup: area, cutout, polyline, count or shape.

rings.description: For create_markup: [[{x,y}, …]] in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, NOT PDF points. An area takes more rings as holes. A vertex may carry `bulge` (tan of a quarter of the arc's sweep, + counter-clockwise; 1 is a half circle) for a true arc to the next vertex, and a ring may be {circle:{cx,cy,r}} with r as a fraction of the page width. Page points are rejected rather than placed off the sheet.

id.description: For delete_markup, reassign_markup and delete_scale_region. Region ids are reported as `scaleRegions` by redbeam_get_ui_state and nowhere else. For get_history: only this markup or scope.

unit.description: For set_calibration: in, ft, mm, cm, m.

lengthPdfPoints.description: For set_calibration: measured length of the reference, in PDF points.

sheet.description: For go_to_page instead of page: the sheet number as the set prints it, e.g. "A4.0". Punctuation and case are ignored ("A.4.0" finds A4.0); a code that matches no sheet, or more than one, is refused rather than guessed.

query.description: For find_text: the text to find, e.g. a tag like "C-7".

wholeWord.description: For find_text: only whole words, so "C-7" does not also find C-70. Default false.

limit.description: For find_text (default 300 matches), get_words (default 3000 words) and get_lines (default 300 lines). get_history: default 200 events. get_piece_list: default 1000 runs.

margin.description: For zoom_to_region: room left around the box, as a fraction of its size. Default 0.15.

highlight.description: For zoom_to_region: mark the box the way a search hit is marked. Default true.

embedded.description: For set_markup_visibility: false hides the PDF's own markups (Bluebeam's or anyone's), true shows them. Omit to leave as is.

redbeam.description: For set_markup_visibility: false hides REDBEAM's takeoff, dimensions and layout drawn over the sheet, true shows them. The takeoff itself is untouched.

points.description: For measure: two or more {x,y} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y down. Nothing is drawn or written.

closed.description: For measure: close the shape back to the first point and also give its area. Default false.

minLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out segments shorter than this, in PDF points. Default 2 (hatching and text strokes).

name.description: For save_copy: the copy's file name. Defaults to "<name> (takeoff).pdf"; a free name is found if it is taken.

productType.description: For create_scope, update_scope and describe_product: panels, planks, baffle_cassette, baffle, linear_parts or custom_assembly. Decides what the scope is measured as, so create_scope needs no scopeType with it. describe_product without it lists every product.

mode.description: For set_pattern_origin: point (start exactly at `point`, inside the area), corner (the area's corner named by `corner`, or the one nearest `point`), edge (the point on the area's edge nearest `point`, so the first member sits on that edge or line), center (the middle of the area), auto (clear it; the layout chooses the best start).

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

applyTo.description: For set_pattern_direction: the whole scope (default), every area of the scope on the sheet showing, or one area (markupId or point). Area beats page beats scope.

angle.description: For set_pattern_direction instead of x1..y2: the direction members run, in degrees on the sheet: 0 across, 90 up it.

create.description: For trace_area: also place the outline as an area of scopeId (or the active scope). Default false: the rings are returned for create_markup.

bridgeGapFeet.description: For trace_area: the widest gap in the linework still treated as closed, in feet. Default 3.5.

dimension.description: For read_scale: a written dimension, e.g. 12'-6", to check the sheet's scale against; give the two ends it spans as `points`.

replaces.description: For track_addenda with `page`: the ZERO-based page this addendum sheet replaces, to link the two by hand.

markups.description: For create_markups: up to 500 entries, each {kind, rings, scopeId?, page?} as create_markup takes them. One undo step.

inside.description: For get_lines: only lines with both ends inside rect. Default false (lines crossing it are included).

angleTolerance.description: For get_lines orientation, in degrees. Default 1.

dedupe.description: For get_lines: merge a segment drawn twice, in either direction. Default true.

sort.description: For get_lines: longest first (default), left to right, or top to bottom.

maxLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out longer segments, in PDF points.

minLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: shortest length kept, in feet.

maxLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: longest length kept, in feet.

withoutEmbeddedMarkups.description: For save_copy: leave every other app's markups (Bluebeam's, anyone's) out of the copy. Links stay. Default false.

path.description: For export: an absolute path to write the file to, e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\Desktop\\takeoff.csv. Its folder must exist. Without it, text formats come back in the reply.

overwrite.description: For export with path: replace a file already there. A PDF is never replaced.
